newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran minister warns Germany over court charges.
newsitem.headline: Iran minister warns Germany over court charges.

text.p: Iran warned its biggest trade partner Germany on Sunday that it would not compromise in a row over German charges that Tehran ordered the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

"We will not compromise with anyone or anything over Islamic values and the values of the Islamic Republic of Iran," Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told Iranian television, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC).

Iran has been engaged in a war of words with Germany since a German prosecutor last week accused Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other Tehran officials of ordering the deaths of three senior Kurdish opposition figures and their translator at a Berlin restaurant in 1992.
Germany was "gravely mistaken" if it thought Iran would ignore such an insult, Velayati said.
Tehran has denied any role in the killings and protested on Thursday to Bonn over the charges.
"In our view, that move is not a judicial one, but a totally political one," Velayati told the television.
About 5,000 Iranian students marched to Germany's embassy in Tehran on Sunday and threw eggs and tomatoes at the compound to protest against the accusations.
In Bonn, the German Foreign Ministry said on Sunday it would keep cool over the row with Iran.
Germany is Iran's leading trade partner. The two countries' trade stood at more than $1.4 billion last year.
German prosecutors on Friday demanded life sentences for an Iranian and a Lebanese who were tried for carrying out the gangland-style shootings.
